GO:0005576.name: extracellular region

definition.text: The space external to the outermost structure of a cell. For cells without external protective or external encapsulating structures this refers to space outside of the plasma membrane. This term covers the host cell environment outside an intracellular parasite.

GO:0005576.comment: Note that this term is intended to annotate gene products that are not attached to the cell surface. For gene products at the cell surface, consider annotating to external side of plasma membrane ; GO:0009897.

definition.text: Binding to an identical protein or proteins.
Binding to a protein.

GO:0030451.name: regulation of complement activation, alternative pathway

definition.text: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of the alternative pathway of complement activation.

synonyms.name: regulation of complement cascade, alternative pathway

definition.text: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of complement activation.
Binding to a heparan sulfate proteoglycan, any proteoglycan containing heparan sulfate as the glycosaminoglycan carbohydrate unit.

GO:0006508.name: proteolysis

definition.text: The hydrolysis of proteins into smaller polypeptides and/or amino acids by cleavage of their peptide bonds.

GO:0006508.comment: This term was intentionally placed under 'protein metabolic process ; GO:0019538' rather than 'protein catabolic process ; GO:0030163' to cover all processes centered on breaking peptide bonds, including those involved in protein processing.

definition.text: Any process involved in the activation of any of the steps of the complement cascade, which allows for the direct killing of microbes, the disposal of immune complexes, and the regulation of other immune processes; the initial steps of complement activation involve one of three pathways, the classical pathway, the alternative pathway, and the lectin pathway, all of which lead to the terminal complement pathway.

Any process involved in the activation of any of the steps of the alternative pathway of the complement cascade which allows for the direct killing of microbes and the regulation of other immune processes.

The immediate defensive reaction (by vertebrate tissue) to infection or injury caused by chemical or physical agents. The process is characterized by local vasodilation, extravasation of plasma into intercellular spaces and accumulation of white blood cells and macrophages.

GO:1905370.name: serine-type endopeptidase complex

definition.text: A protein complex which is capable of serine-type endopeptidase activity.

GO:1905370.comment: An example of this is PLAU in human (UniProt symbol P00749) in PMID:1689240 (inferred from direct assay).

definition.text: A phospholipid microvesicle that is derived from any of several cell types, such as platelets, blood cells, endothelial cells, or others, and contains membrane receptors as well as other proteins characteristic of the parental cell. Microparticles are heterogeneous in size, and are characterized as microvesicles free of nucleic acids.

A vesicle that is released into the extracellular region by fusion of the limiting endosomal membrane of a multivesicular body with the plasma membrane. Extracellular exosomes, also simply called exosomes, have a diameter of about 40-100 nm.

Binding to heparin, a member of a group of glycosaminoglycans found mainly as an intracellular component of mast cells and which consist predominantly of alternating alpha-(1->4)-linked D-galactose and N-acetyl-D-glucosamine-6-sulfate residues.
The cell surface of a secondary, endosymbiont organism with which the first organism is interacting. The symbiont is defined as the smaller of the organisms involved in a symbiotic interaction.
Binding to a C3b product of the complement cascade.
Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of complement-dependent cytotoxicity.
The cellular developmental process in which a specific cell progresses from an immature to a mature state. Cell development start once cell commitment has taken place.
Generation of cells within the nervous system.

The process in which neuronal axons and dendrites become coated with a segmented lipid-rich sheath (myelin) to enable faster and more energetically efficient conduction of electrical impulses. The sheath is formed by the cell membranes of oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system. Adjacent myelin segments are separated by a non-myelinated stretch of axon called a node of Ranvier.
Binding to a glycan (polysaccharide) containing a substantial proportion of aminomonosaccharide residues.
Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of the inflammatory response.

GO:0045957.name: negative regulation of complement activation, alternative pathway

definition.text: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of complement activation by the alternative pathway.

synonyms.name: down regulation of complement activation, alternative pathway
down-regulation of complement activation, alternative pathway
downregulation of complement activation, alternative pathway
inhibition of complement activation, alternative pathway
negative regulation of complement cascade, alternative pathway

definition.text: Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of complement activation.
Binding to a C3d product of the complement cascade.
Any process that stops, prevents or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of complement-dependent cytotoxicity.

GO:0001864.name: pentraxin binding

definition.text: Binding to a pentraxin, a member of a family of inflammatory proteins with a radially symmetric arrangement of five identical, noncovalently linked chains in a pentagonal array.

GO:0001864.comment: Note that pentraxins include such proteins as serum amyloid P component (SAP) and C-reactive protein (CRP).

genuine author manuscript; selected full Methods/Results. Selected locations: manuscript lines 123–194,295–375; Figures 3–5. Exact target/source linkage checked; assay scope is stated in the annotation review.
